findings.claim: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now(), which is evaluated once at class definition/import time. Every instance created without an explicit value therefore shares the same stale timestamp instead of getting its own creation time.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a plain dataclass default, so it is evaluated once at import; `from_integration` (lines 22-25) never passes `queued`, so every instance gets the process-import timestamp. Nothing in src/sentry currently reads `.queued`, so the stale value is only serialised via `to_dict`.

findings.claim: to_dict() uses asdict(), which leaves queued as a datetime object. Serializing the dict to JSON as task kwargs can raise TypeError.

verifier.reason: `to_dict()` does return `asdict(self)` with `queued` still a `datetime` (src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:27-28), but task kwargs are not JSON-serialized: Celery is configured with `CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"` and `CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = {"pickle"}` (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741). A `datetime` pickles fine and passes the bad-pickle guard, which rejects only Django models and `sentry.`/`getsentry.` classes (src/sentry/celery.py:49-56), so no TypeError is raised.

findings.claim: from_dict does not type-check or convert queued on deserialisation, so under a JSON serializer it comes back as a str.

verifier.reason: from_dict does pass queued through unconverted (src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31-35), but the str outcome cannot occur here: Celery is configured for pickle only (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741), so the datetime round-trips intact. Nothing in src/ ever reads .queued, so the JSON-serializer scenario is hypothetical.

verifier.reason: tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:13 defines `test_from_dict_inalid_data`, added by the patch (change.patch line 277); it sits beside `test_from_dict_valid_data` and passes invalid data, so `invalid` was clearly intended.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `assignment_source` to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411-418, but the only non-test caller (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:44-46) passes just three positional arguments. No implementation reads it: jira/integration.py:990, jira_server/integration.py:1090, vsts/issues.py:266 and example/integration.py:161 never reference `assignment_source`.

verifier.reason: The two abstract methods are inconsistent, but in the opposite direction to the claim's wording: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411-418 adds `assignment_source` to abstract `sync_status_outbound` (never passed by any caller), while abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` at issues.py:397-403 does not declare it, even though src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59-61 passes `assignment_source=` to it and it is only absorbed by `**kwargs`.

findings.claim: Status-sync cycles are not protected. tasks/sync_status_outbound.py calls should_sync("outbound_status") without a source argument, so only assignee sync gets loop protection.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_status")` with no source and the task takes no source argument (line 19), so the same-integration check at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 never fires for status sync; only sync_assignee_outbound.py:56 passes a source. The patch adds an `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` (issues.py:416) but nothing ever supplies it.

verifier.reason: The only matching-source test added is for assign (tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:203-221); the deassign test at :273-276 passes no source and asserts assignment_source=None. test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign (:349-388) does reach deassign with a matching source via sync.py:96-99, but runs outside self.tasks() and never asserts the outbound sync is suppressed.

findings.claim: The new task kwarg assignment_source_dict causes TypeError on old workers during a rolling deploy, so assignee sync is lost.

verifier.reason: The patch adds the parameter (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:34) and in the same change makes the caller always send the `assignment_source_dict` key, even when None (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141), so a worker still on the old three-argument signature raises TypeError on every such task. "Lost" is overstated: the `retry` wrapper catches it and re-queues (src/sentry/tasks/base.py:170-172) with a 5-minute delay and 5 retries, so sync is dropped only if old workers outlast that window.

findings.claim: from_dict catches TypeError/ValueError and returns None without logging or emitting a metric, so a malformed payload silently disables loop protection.

verifier.reason: `from_dict` at src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31-35 catches `(ValueError, TypeError)` and returns None with no log or metric; src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56 passes that None to `should_sync`, whose cycle check at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 is skipped when `sync_source` is falsy, so the outbound sync proceeds. In practice the dict only comes from `to_dict()`, so this needs schema drift between deploys to trigger.

findings.claim: source_name is serialised into every task payload but never read; should_sync compares only integration_id.

verifier.reason: `source_name` is declared and populated in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:16,23 and serialised via `to_dict()` into the task kwargs at src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py (`assignment_source_dict`), but a grep of `src/` finds no other read of it; `should_sync` in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py compares only `sync_source.integration_id`. The payload carries it only when an assignment source is set (otherwise `None`), so this is an unused field, not a behavioural bug.

findings.claim: The loop guard compares integration IDs rather than external issues, so an inbound reassignment no longer propagates between two external issues linked to the same group on the same integration.

verifier.reason: The guard at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 returns False whenever `sync_source.integration_id` equals the installation's integration ID, and src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:135-145 passes that same source to every external issue linked to the group. A sibling external issue on the same integration is therefore skipped at src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:56, where before the patch it was synced; src/sentry/models/grouplink.py:82 allows several such links per group.
